simple.meaning: עֶוֶל (ʻevel) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “(moral) evil.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 54 times across Leviticus, Deuteronomy, 2 Samuel, 1 Chronicles, 2 Chronicles, and 11 more, beginning at Leviticus 19:15. Its contexts include righteousness, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עֶוֶל (H5766).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: עֶוֶל (ʻevel) / H5766 is traced through Leviticus 19:15, Leviticus 19:35, Deuteronomy 25:16, Deuteronomy 32:4 as a generated source-based concept entry.

occurrences.englishText: “ ‘You shall do no injustice in judgment. You shall not be partial to the poor, nor show favoritism to the great; but you shall judge your neighbor in righteousness.

For all who do such things, all who do unrighteously, are an abomination to Yahweh your God.
The Rock: his work is perfect,
Your hands weren’t bound, and your feet weren’t put into fetters. As a man falls before the children of iniquity, so you fell.”

Please return.
